direction: Steering Evo2-7B (a DNA generative model) to control the α-helical content of the protein encoded by its generated DNA, via targeted internal interventions, while preserving sequence validity

behaviors.statement: Under a targeted internal intervention during decoding, Evo2-7B generates DNA whose encoded protein has a significantly higher α-helical fraction than the unintervened baseline, while remaining a valid ORF.
behaviors.behavior_conclusion: Confirmed achievable and quantified: a single-direction contrastive-activation-addition (CAA) steer at Evo2-7B residual block 28 raises the mean α-helix fraction of generated ORFs from a 0.414 baseline to 0.482 at a conservative coefficient (and up to ~0.575, +0.16, at higher coefficients), dose-dependently and direction-specifically, with validity non-inferior at the conservative setting. The gain trades off against validity and co-occurs with GC/protein-length shifts as the coefficient increases, so the achievable 'high-helix + valid' regime is the low-coefficient knee of a dose–validity Pareto frontier.

mechanisms.family: Representation and Parameter Analysis / Steering Vectors (CAA)
mechanisms.headline: A single residual-stream direction at Evo2-7B block 28, built by contrastive activation addition (mean high-helix − mean low-helix activation), causally raises encoded-protein α-helix dose-dependently (permutation trend ρ=0.922, BH-FDR q=1.5e-4; +0.068 at coef 1.0, +0.161 at coef 4), is direction-specific (matched-control −0.024 n.s. and same-norm sham −0.005 n.s. show no gain; CAA exceeds both p≤1e-6), and reproduces under a within-Evo2-family model swap (evo2_7b_262k, ρ=0.878). Notably, linear probes localize the property only weakly (per-layer R²≈0 or negative) yet the causal CAA lever works, and the Goodfire L26 SAE-clamp arm fails outright (helix decreases with clamp, ρ=−0.95, SAE recon_rel_error≈1.0). The helix gain co-occurs with a GC (−0.139) and protein-length (−37%) shift that also transfers to the swapped checkpoint — a robust family-level property of this lever, though C1's gain survives length-matching and shows no aa-composition bias.

claims.statement: CAA steering along a single Evo2-7B residual direction (block 28) raises the α-helix fraction of the encoded protein above the unintervened baseline with a monotone dose-response.
claims.method: Permutation dose-response trend test on the all-generations helix endpoint (ESMFold→DSSP, invalid→0, TEST split) over a coefficient grid, with matched-control and same-norm sham perturbations for specificity and BH-FDR across sites/coefficients; robustness stress-tested by a within-family model swap.
claims.conclusion: Robustly supported: significant positive dose-response (ρ=0.922, q=1.5e-4; +0.068 helix at coef 1.0, up to +0.16 at coef 4), direction-specific (both controls show no gain), and reproduced under a model swap to evo2_7b_262k (verify robustness 1.00); the per-generation effect is modest (Cliff's δ=0.135) though its CI excludes zero.

claims.statement: At the conservative C1-winning coefficient, steered generations remain valid at a rate non-inferior to baseline, though other sequence properties (GC content, protein length) shift.
claims.method: One-sided non-inferiority test on validity rate over the full generated set (pre-registered margin −0.05) at the winning setting, plus off-target comparison (β-sheet, GC, Evo2 NLL, length, aa-composition) and a validity frontier across the coefficient sweep.
claims.conclusion: Supported but narrowed: validity is non-inferior at coefficients ≤1 (0.968 vs 0.991 baseline, one-sided 95% LB −0.035 > −0.05) but fails the margin at coefficients ≥2 (dose–validity Pareto); GC (−0.139) and protein length (−37%) shift substantially as documented, CAA-specific off-targets — the Stage-1 audit passed with a WARN on the original 'off-target not degraded' wording (since corrected) and the Stage-2 swap-test was deferred under the max_verify_claims cap.
